notes.text: Note from the #151 second-pass review: the wiki baseline on main is now 7 stale pages, not 5 — `features/review-loop.md` (yours from #160) and `features/web-board.md` are stale at main. Re-stamp both as part of this card.

Full review of PR #175 for the continuation attempt:

The work is correct and well tested — 768 tests, smoke green; the fast-forward really ends at the remote head with a working plain push (driven through five scenarios: human-ahead, diverged, local-ahead, remote unreachable, no remote); divergence is reported as `stale` rather than forced; trigger mode records only `continues_pr`; the 1,680-char reason reaches the brief whole; three of the four nits taken.

**Must do — the PR is CONFLICTING with main** (it was cut before #150 / PR #152 merged, 57c8b9a). Two content conflicts: `src/dispatch.js` in `spawnWorker` — main replaced `const env = {` with `const env = profile.mode === 'claude-bg' ? scrubKbEnv(process.env) : {` on the line right after your `const continued = …` — keep both; and `docs/wiki/log.md` — keep both entries. Merge origin/main, do not rebase.

**In the same pass:**
1. After the merge, `features/review-loop.md` and `features/operator-seat.md` will be stale again (main's model.js/dispatch.js/lifecycle.js/cli.js blobs already differ from what you stamped). Re-run `node .repolore/scripts/wiki-check.mjs` after merging, re-verify the review-loop prose still holds with `scrubKbEnv` in `spawnWorker`, and re-stamp both.
2. `docs/wiki/features/review-loop.md` ~166-170 (Known gaps) says a silent fetch failure makes the ff-only merge fail too, so the checkout is reported stale. Measured the opposite: with a tracking ref present, the ff-only succeeds against the stale ref ("Already up to date") and the checkout is reported clean although the remote may be ahead; only the no-tracking-ref case reports stale. Rewrite the sentence to say that.

Nits, take what is cheap: `src/board.js` ~340 — a repo with no `<remote>/<branch>` ref is labelled stale and the brief tells the worker to reset to a remote that does not exist; a `git rev-parse --verify --quiet <remote>/<branch>` first separates "nothing to fast-forward to" from "diverged" (the existing test at test/dispatch.test.js ~429 now silently exercises that path). `src/board.js` ~319 — the reuse-existing-worktree branch returns `stale: null` without attempting the ff. `src/cli.js` ~496 — `hkb claim --spawn` records `continues_branch` but not `continues_branch_stale`. `src/dispatch.js` ~837 — the trigger-mode claim log line says nothing about continuing a PR. `src/board.js` ~308 doc comment: local-only commits with an unchanged remote are not stale, only true divergence is.

Same branch, same PR (worktree-kb-162-1). Rerun lint/test/smoke, then `hkb finish`.

results.summary: Continued PR #175 per the reviewer's must-do: merged origin/main (kept both sides of the src/dispatch.js spawnWorker conflict — the continued-branch stale reporting plus scrubKbEnv from #150 — and both docs/wiki/log.md entries). Then addressed the review's remaining items: worktreeOnBranch's reuse-existing-worktree path (a spawn that died between checkout and launch) now fetches and fast-forwards too instead of trusting the leftover checkout; a shared fastForwardToRemote helper checks for the <remote>/<branch> tracking ref with git rev-parse --verify --quiet before the ff-only merge, so a branch this host has never fetched reports 'no <remote>/<branch> ref to catch up to' distinctly from a real divergence; the doc comment now says local-only commits ahead of an unchanged remote are never stale on their own; hkb claim --spawn records continues_branch_stale like the dispatcher's own claim; and the claim loop's log line for a trigger-mode continuation still names the PR it continues even though it makes no checkout. Rewrote review-loop.md's Known-gaps sentence to match what was actually measured (a silent fetch failure against an existing tracking ref reports clean, not stale; only a fetch that never created the ref reports stale), re-stamped review-loop.md and operator-seat.md (anchors moved again from the merge) and web-board.md (no-op) after the merge.
